10.1b — 2-Button Jam: Build Day 1

Build Day 1 rule: end the day with the core loop — BOTH verbs working, something to act on, a lose state. Ugly is fine; non-playable is not. A jam that leaves Day 1 without its loop spends Day 3 building the loop instead of the game.

Build Day ~50 min

Build order (the loop skeleton):

  1. Read both inputs — one line each, GetKeyDown. Print to console on press. Nothing else works until this does:
if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.LeftArrow)) Debug.Log("A");
if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.RightArrow)) Debug.Log("B");
  1. Verb 1 with a placeholder — say DUCK: scale the player sprite to 0.5 height. One line of code, instantly testable, already FUN to spam.
  2. Verb 2 with a placeholder — DASH: a 0.15s Translate burst in facing direction. Your 3.3 cooldown pattern IS the dash (it is a fire rate on a movement).
  3. Something to act on — one obstacle, one pickup, one enemy. ANY one. Borrow the starter's spike or coin prefab wholesale.
  4. One lose state — the death loop you have written twice (2.2); here it can just be "restart the scene."

Checkpoint ritual (last 10 minutes): pass the keyboard around the team — each member plays the loop for 30 seconds. Anyone who cannot play it cannot build on it.

Close of Day ~5 min

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Play your own loop: both verbs, one obstacle, one lose state
  • Explain the build order and why inputs print before mechanics
  • Name your riskiest task for Day 2
